clue.text: Pudding where we'd expect to see tea, it's said

definitions.text: Pudding where we'd expect to see tea, it's said

parts.words: Pudding where we'd expect to see tea, it's said
parts.note: 'tea' spoken is the letter T; the dessert course likewise comes after the main dish

explanation.surface: Someone describes a dessert served at the point in the day where tea would normally come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' tells you to hear 'tea' as the letter T; the place you expect T is just past S in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for the dessert course that follows the main meal.

clue.text: One furnishes capital home with more elaborate fencing

indicators.note: to fence something is to enclose it, so the word for more elaborate surrounds the word for home

parts.note: fancier means more ornate or elaborate
in means at home

explanation.surface: A householder furnishes the place in the capital with fancier railings.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer who provides the money, or capital, for a business venture.

clue.text: Allude to trapping beast coming up from foreign parts

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the word for allude to holds the beast inside it

parts.note: to cite is to refer or allude to
an ox is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: Someone mentions a strange animal arriving from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trapping' puts the beast inside; 'coming up' then reads the whole from bottom to top, so the beast ends up backwards too.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic things are introduced from abroad, originating in distant lands.

clue.text: Take out child, heading off after school on vacation

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first
vacated means emptied, so the word school loses all its inner letters
the first letter, its head, is taken off the word for child

parts.note: a daughter is a female child

explanation.surface: A child is taken out of school for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' empties SCHOOL to SL; 'heading off' cuts DAUGHTER to AUGHTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To take out, in slang, is to kill; slaughter means kill in large numbers.

clue.text: What some solicitors do on hearing a charge

indicators.note: the phrase for a charge is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a cost is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A lawyer's work as a criminal charge is heard in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitors' looks legal, but here they are streetwalkers, who approach passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Prostitutes soliciting trade approach and proposition strangers in the street.

clue.text: Democrat moving in to make changes for promoters

indicators.note: the Democrat's letter shifts further into the word rather than staying where it is

parts.note: to amend is to make changes
D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: A politician joins a team to shake up campaign publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising people promote products and services.

clue.text: Merry monarch's order for salad?

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme
a law is an order or decree

explanation.surface: A jolly king demands a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is the 'merry old soul' of a nursery rhyme; his order would be Cole's law.
explanation.definitionFit: Shredded raw cabbage dressed with mayonnaise is a classic side salad.

clue.text: Countryman to consider keeping wife and daughter apart

indicators.note: the word for consider holds the other letters within it
the wife's and daughter's letters go in at separate places, kept apart

parts.note: to see is to consider

explanation.surface: A man thinks about separating his wife and daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes after the first letter of SEE and D after the second, kept apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede is a native of Sweden, a countryman in the sense of a national.

clue.text: Lady from Lisbon hears no evil

indicators.note: evil letters are corrupted, so the letters of hears no are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Portuguese woman follows the proverb about hearing no evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Portuguese form of address equivalent to Mrs or madam, so a Portuguese lady.

clue.text: Young peers happily sharing a mistress?

definitions.text: Young peers happily sharing a mistress?

parts.words: Young peers happily sharing a mistress?
parts.note: the scandalous picture is really of pupils who share one schoolmistress as their teacher

explanation.surface: Young aristocrats contentedly share a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' suggests lords and 'mistress' a lover; really they are children of the same age with one teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellow pupils, peers of the same age taught at the same place.

clue.text: Most equable ladies regularly appearing in film

indicators.note: the chosen letters show up inside the word for film

parts.note: a mist is a thin film or haze

indicators.note: taking every other letter of ladies, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Women keep turning up in the calmest of movies.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of mild: the gentlest, most even-tempered.

clue.text: Result of making mini bats for children's game?

parts.note: tiddly is British informal for very small
to bat an eye is to wink, so bats means winks

explanation.surface: Making little cricket bats results in a children's pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like sports equipment, but it is the verb, as in batting an eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: A game played by flicking small plastic counters into a cup.

clue.text: Putting self-portrait on display, bashfully

definitions.meaning: an artist hanging a picture of their own head on a wall
acting in a shamefaced, embarrassed way, with eyes lowered

explanation.definitionFit: Lowering the face in shame or shyness is the posture of someone embarrassed.

clue.text: Skip university in pursuit of love

indicators.note: following behind, so the university comes after love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone skips university while chasing romance.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip something is to leave it out.

clue.text: Patriots withdrawing singular honour for Hollywood legend?

indicators.note: drawing back, so the word for patriots is read backwards

parts.note: Nats is short for nationalists, ardent patriots
laurels are honours; one, in the singular, is a laurel

explanation.surface: Nationalists retract a unique award for a film star.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy, a screen great.

clue.text: Uneasy and unready to receive, getting out

definitions.meaning: ill at ease, uncomfortable in a situation
declining to see visitors, as a householder might tell callers

explanation.definitionFit: Being uncomfortable, refusing callers, and simply being absent are all expressed by the idiom.

clue.text: Careers madly round house for something to put shirt on?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation for house
wild, crazy movement means the letters of careers are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tears frantically around the house hunting a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: To put your shirt on something is British slang for betting everything you have on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse bred for racing, the classic object of an all-or-nothing bet.

clue.text: Breed of dog, one lean aggressive type

parts.note: the pug is a small snub-nosed dog breed
I is the Roman numeral one
to list is to lean, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A particular dog breed, one lean and fierce.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer, someone who fights with fists.

clue.text: French madame and monsieur have words before ceremony

parts.note: to have words is to argue
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A French couple quarrel before their wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French madame' looks like part of the couple, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A common French woman's first name, so a typical French lady.

clue.text: Boat from south Jersey or Guernsey?

parts.note: both are breeds of dairy cow, named after Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A boat sails from the south of one Channel Island or another.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey and Guernsey are Channel Islands and also cattle breeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed barge, a type of boat.

clue.text: Bird going up rubbish heap gets very little to eat

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top
the heap swallows the small word inside it

parts.note: a tip is a British rubbish dump
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A bird flies up from a dump with a scrap of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To eat' puts the small word inside the heap; 'going up' reverses the whole result, as this is a down clue. A tip is a British rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the lapwing, after its call.

clue.text: Gather where beaver's seen and weather the storm

parts.note: to take it is to gather or infer
beaver is old slang for a beard, which grows on the chin

explanation.surface: Someone gathers where a beaver lives and rides out bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaver' is dated slang for a beard, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept a blow or setback stoically, enduring hardship.

clue.text: Japanese art, complete with fine raised frame

indicators.note: the raised pair of letters forms a frame around the word for complete
in a down entry, raised means turned upwards

parts.note: OK means fine
to end is to complete

explanation.surface: A Japanese painting is finished with a good upright frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords.

clue.text: Eastern firm set up by an Indian, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means placed upward, reversed

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An Asian company founded by someone from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' suggests a person, but it is the Indian Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian is one example of the world's great seas.

clue.text: Nurses treated current stabbing early in the day

indicators.note: the current's letter is driven into the rearranged letters
treated, worked over, so the letters of nurses are rearranged

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Nurses tend an electric shock wound first thing in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated' rearranges NURSES to SUNRSE, and I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn, the start of the morning when the sun appears.

clue.text: Sailor looking fatigued aboard, running back and forth

indicators.note: on board, so the sailor's letters go around the other word

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for ordinary seaman

indicators.note: the word for looking fatigued runs backwards

parts.note: drawn means looking tired and strained

explanation.surface: A weary sailor dashes up and down the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And forth' looks like part of 'back and forth', but 'forth' alone is the definition; 'running back' reverses only the fatigued word, which goes 'aboard' the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in direction or time, as in 'from that day forth'.

clue.text: Playwright once releasing book to be grabbed by males ready for casting?

indicators.note: the shortened playwright is held inside the word for males

parts.note: men are males

indicators.note: letting go, so the book's letter is dropped

parts.note: Robert Bolt, the late writer of A Man for All Seasons

explanation.surface: A dramatist loses his script and is collared by actors at an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting' suggests theatre auditions, but it means pouring metal into a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal liquefied by heat can be poured into a mould.

clue.text: Judge from Spain comes across the wrong way

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: facing the wrong way, so the word for comes across is read backwards

parts.note: meets means comes across

explanation.surface: A Spanish judge encounters something backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem is to consider or reckon, as in 'I esteem it an honour'.
